office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Two-term Republican Rep. Stephanie McClintock, a former Battle Ground School Board member, faces Democrat Randi L. Knott, a first-time candidate with a public-policy career; they split most clearly on the tax on income over $1 million, which McClintock voted against and Knott supports.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate with more than 25 years of public-policy work, a former Brush Prairie bed-and-breakfast and horse-ranch owner, and a disability advocate, running on affordability, special-education funding and health care.
highlights: Says the ultra-wealthy need to be taxed and called the millionaire tax bill "drafted very well" [S6]
Calls for fully funded special education and infrastructure investments that keep pace with growth [S3]
Says health care is a human right and supports universal health-care solutions [S3]
Serves on the Clark County Developmental Disabilities Advisory Board; has not held elected office [S1][S4]

taxes.basis: Says the ultra-wealthy need to be taxed to fund schools and praises the millionaire tax bill; pamphlet opposes policies that protect the wealthy and big corporations.

spending.basis: Calls for fully funded special education, infrastructure investment and restored Medicaid funding, framed as 'economically progressive policies that are fiscally responsible.'

healthcare.basis: Calls health care a human right and supports 'universal healthcare solutions that reduce cost and complexity', without naming a single-payer system.

experience.basis: First-time candidate running against a two-term incumbent, though with a long public-policy career and board appointments.

candidates.summary: Two-term Republican incumbent, ranking member on House Consumer Protection and Business and former Battle Ground School Board member, running on lower taxes, law enforcement and K-12 accountability.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O and transportation revenue bills [S5][S6][S7]
Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget and the 2026 supplemental budget [S8][S9]
Campaigns on law-enforcement funding, restoring police pursuit and sex-offender registration bills [S1][S2][S13]
Co-sponsored HB 1699 on sex-separated girls' school sports and voted against ESHB 1296, which amended the 2024 parents' rights law [S11][S14]
Endorsed by The Columbian editorial board [S16]

taxes.basis: Voted against ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5801, co-sponsored bills repealing 2025 tax increases, and says she opposes the income tax.

spending.basis: Voted against both operating budgets and pledges to oppose 'reckless spending' and demand accountability, while naming special education and Medicaid as budget priorities.

housing.basis: Voted against EHB 1217, the 2025 limit on residential rent and fee increases.

safety.basis: Calls for fully funding law enforcement and restoring police pursuit; prime-sponsored sex-offender registration bills and co-sponsored encampment-removal funding.

social.basis: Co-sponsored HB 1699, letting schools bar biologically male students from girls' sports; no recorded position on abortion or gender-affirming care.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296, which amended the parents' rights enacted by I-2081, and describes herself as a champion of parental involvement as a school director.

tech.basis: Says AI is better handled federally and that differing state regulations create challenges for businesses.

experience.basis: Two-term incumbent, ranking committee member and former school director with an enacted prime-sponsored bill (SHB 1121).
